gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that diagonal translation of x, y, and z fails to regularize independent spatial directions, so the claimed smoothness and derivative estimates are unavailable; the prediction also gives the corresponding full-space mollifier repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The diagonal spatial convolution leaves transverse spatial directions unchanged and therefore does not produce the smooth regularization required by the proof.

component_coverage.gold_component: The diagonal spatial averaging does not smooth all 3d spatial variables, allowing a Lipschitz but nonsmooth transverse dependence to survive and invalidating the derivative-based proof.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies the diagonal shift set, supplies a surviving nonsmooth x-y dependence, states the resulting failure of smoothness and derivative estimates, and specifies independent R^{3d} mollification.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns evaluating the time-shifted mollification outside v's declared time domain near t=1 and repairing that temporal-domain gap. ISSUE-001 concerns a separate spatial diagonal-kernel defect; its mention of v's domain does not identify the missing terminal-time extension or restricted comparison interval.

The gold issue is the failure to obtain a uniform consistency modulus over the varying comparison family, while ISSUE-003 identifies only an unsupported all-n quantifier and missing control for finitely many large-h cases. It does not diagnose the absent uniformity needed for scalar E1 and E2 bounds.

Both identify that piecewise-constant u_h can jump by order h^{1/2}, so time convolution cannot be bounded by O(epsilon) alone; the lower comparison bound therefore needs an epsilon+h^{1/2} term and adjusted constants.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof incorrectly omits the h^{1/2} temporal-grid jump contribution when estimating the uniform difference between u_h and its mollification.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed O(epsilon) mollification error for piecewise-constant u_h is invalid because grid jumps contribute an additional order-h^{1/2} term, requiring correction of the lower comparison bound and dependent constants.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies the grid-point jumps, explains why convolution across them produces O(h^{1/2}) error, rejects the epsilon-only bound, and supplies the corrected epsilon+h^{1/2} estimate.
